The phone-intake module does not make outbound sales calls. It does not give medical or legal advice, and it does not take card payments by phone. If a caller asks for any of these, the module explains that a person will follow up.

The modules did not stop every no-show, and the report did not promise that they would. The salon still decided its own cancellation policy. Card payments by phone were out of scope for phone-intake, so deposits stayed a manual step.

# AI phone intake

The phone-intake module answers incoming calls out of hours and in peak times, records the request, and books or passes it on. It is built for businesses where the phone rings while every member of staff is busy with a customer.

rows.question: Can ticket-creation mark a job as finished by itself?

contexts.text:
# Ticket creation

The ticket-creation module turns each accepted request into a ticket with the fields the team needs, and tracks its status. It sits after intake: once a request has been accepted, the module makes sure it becomes a job that someone owns.

## What is not included

The ticket-creation module does not close a ticket without a person. A member of staff marks the job done. It does not do billing; invoices stay in your existing system.

## Who it suits

Owners who write jobs on paper or in a spreadsheet and then lose track of which ones are done usually pair this module with phone-intake or email-triage. The ticket is the single place where the job lives.

## What it does

For each accepted request, the module creates a ticket and fills in the fields your team has agreed on, such as customer, address, request type and requested date. Before it creates a ticket it checks for duplicates, so the same request sent twice does not become two jobs. It then tracks the ticket's status from open to done and reminds staff when a ticket has not moved.

## Connecting it to your tools

The module works with csv-export, api-connector and crm-connector. The crm-connector maps ticket fields to the fields in your CRM, so a ticket created here appears as a record there.

rows.answer: No. According to the knowledge base, the ticket-creation module does not close a ticket without a person. A member of staff marks the job done. The module creates tickets, fills in the agreed fields, checks for duplicates, and tracks status from open to done, reminding staff when a ticket has not moved, but the final "done" step is taken by a staff member.

rows.question: What happens if my daily workload is larger than the top tier?

contexts.text:
## Above the top tier

Above 150 requests per day there is no automatic estimate and a person prices it. The assistant will tell you that the number is outside the rate card and that someone will contact you, rather than showing a figure.

## Why volume matters

The modules do more work when more requests come in: more calls answered, more messages labelled, more tickets checked for duplicates. The tiers keep the price proportionate without pricing each request one by one.

## The table

| Daily requests | Volume factor |
|---|---|
| up to 20 per day | 1.00 |
| up to 60 per day | 1.25 |
| up to 150 per day | 1.50 |
| above 150 per day | no automatic estimate; a person prices it |

# Volume tiers

Your daily request volume changes the monthly price of every module you choose. The change is a multiplier, called the volume factor, taken from a short table. This article shows the table and how to read it.

## How to read it

Find the row that your normal daily volume falls into, and multiply each module's base price by the factor in that row. A business with volume up to 20 requests a day pays the base price with no change. A business with volume up to 60 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.25. A business with volume up to 150 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.50.

The monthly price for each chosen module is its base price multiplied by the volume factor for your daily request volume. The integration surcharges for the integrations you use are added once a month. The setup fee is 900 USD for each module and is paid once. | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| indicative | every pricing input was given by you and nothing conflicts |
| scenario | an input is missing or unknown, and the estimate uses a stated assumption |
| blocked | two of your answers conflict, and no number is shown until you resolve it |

An indicative estimate means that every field the price depends on was reported or confirmed by you and no conflict exists. A scenario estimate means that at least one input is missing, so the assistant has filled it with an assumption that it shows next to the number. MILO prices are arithmetic, not negotiation. Every estimate is built from a published rate card, and the same inputs always give the same number. This article explains the parts of the calculation so that you can check any estimate yourself.

Find the row that your normal daily volume falls into, and multiply each module's base price by the factor in that row. A business with volume up to 20 requests a day pays the base price with no change. A business with volume up to 60 requests a day pays the base price multiplied by 1.25. rows.question: Does a file-based link keep my software permanently connected?

contexts.text:
## How it works

Your tool exports a CSV file, for example the list of bookings or jobs for the day. The module reads that file, does its work, and writes a CSV file back. Your tool imports that file. The exchange runs on a schedule you choose, such as every hour or at the end of the day. There is no live connection between the two systems.

## What you need

Your tool must be able to export and import CSV files. Most spreadsheets, booking widgets and small job tools can. During setup we agree the column names on both sides so that the files always line up.

# CSV export and import

The csv-export integration is the simplest way to connect a module to the tool you already use. It needs no live connection, no access key and no change to your tool. This article explains how it works and when it is the right choice.

## The problem

With an export-only tool, a module can read what is in your system, but it cannot write a new record back. Results must be re-keyed or pushed through a file drop. Many trades businesses are in this position: the tool was chosen years ago, the data is in it, and there is no API and no import.

# API connector

The api-connector integration gives a module a live connection to your tool. Bookings, labels, tickets and status changes are written and read as they happen, with no files in between.

rows.answer:
No. A file-based link (the csv-export integration) is not a permanent or live connection. Your tool exports a CSV file, the module reads it, does its work, and writes a CSV file back, which your tool imports. The exchange runs on a schedule you choose, such as hourly or at the end of the day, and there is no live connection between the two systems. It also needs no access key and no change to your tool.

If you need records to update in real time, the api-connector integration gives a live connection instead, with bookings, labels, tickets and status changes written and read as they happen.

## Which modules support it

The api-connector is available for phone-intake, email-triage, ticket-creation and customer-status-updates. It is not offered for staff-assignment, which uses csv-export, or for document-data-entry, which uses csv-export or export-only-tool.
